paperTitle: COEXIST: An Interactive Story Decision-Making Game for Mental Health Awareness
centralContribution: This work presents COEXIST, a short, interactive story decision-making game designed to increase mental health awareness, specifically focusing on self-care as a form of prevention for mental disorders such as depression and social isolation.

elements.name: COEXIST Game
elements.description: A short, interactive story decision-making game designed to increase mental health awareness, specifically focusing on self-care as a form of prevention for mental disorders.
elements.justification: This is the central contribution and the core artifact presented by the paper, encompassing the entire system and its purpose.

elements.name: Mr Shadow (Depression Metaphor)
elements.description: A black humanoid clone of the protagonist (Fig. 1) that serves as a metaphor for depression, dynamically shrinking or growing based on the protagonist's choices.
elements.justification: It is the primary visual and mechanical antagonist, directly illustrating the severity of depression within the game's narrative, and is explicitly linked to Fig. 1.

elements.name: Freytag's Pyramid Narrative Structure
elements.description: The five-stage narrative framework (Exposition, Rising Action, Climax, Falling Action, Resolution) that structures the game's entire story progression (Fig. 2).
elements.justification: This structure is fundamental to the game's narrative design and emotional arc, defining how the story unfolds, and is explicitly shown in Fig. 2.

elements.name: Scoring System (Blue/Red Butterflies)
elements.description: An internal game mechanic that visibly tracks the protagonist's mental health progress using blue (positive) and red (depressive) butterflies, directly influencing Mr Shadow's size.
elements.justification: It provides clear, real-time feedback to the player on the impact of their choices and is integral to the game's core loop, linking directly to Mr Shadow's transformation.

elements.name: Protagonist Character
elements.description: A socially isolated 3D humanoid character, colored in ice white, whose struggles with depression and daily decisions form the core of the game's interactive narrative.
elements.justification: The player experiences the game through this character, making their journey and mental state central to the game's emotional impact and educational purpose.

elements.name: Dynamic Environment & Soundtrack
elements.description: The game's visual environment (darkening/brightening) and background music (heavier/livelier) adapt in real-time to reflect the protagonist's deteriorating or improving mental state.
elements.justification: These elements enhance player immersion and provide continuous, non-verbal feedback on the protagonist's mental health, reinforcing the narrative's emotional weight.

elements.name: Decision-Making Gameplay
elements.description: The interactive core of COEXIST where players make choices during the protagonist's daily routine, directly influencing their mental state and the narrative's path.
elements.justification: This mechanism is how the game engages players, allowing them to actively explore the consequences of self-care choices and understand mental health impacts.

elements.name: Climax Scene (Protagonist Collapse)
elements.description: The narrative's peak moment where the protagonist collapses exhausted on the floor, with Mr Shadow standing impassively by (Fig. 5), designed to reinforce depression awareness.
elements.justification: This critical moment visually emphasizes the severity of depression and its impact, forming a pivotal emotional point in the narrative and is explicitly linked to Fig. 5.

elements.name: Resolution End Scenes (Victory/Defeat)
elements.description: Two distinct visual outcomes: 'victory of depression' (lifeless garden, enlarged Mr Shadow, Fig. 6a) or 'victory over depression' (lively garden, shrunken Mr Shadow, Fig. 6b).
elements.justification: These final visual states summarize the player's journey and reinforce the game's core message about the consequences of choices, directly referenced with Fig. 6a and 6b.
